name: Numerical Benchmarks for the Operational Criteria of Self-Modeling Dynamics
description: This is a companion computational benchmark to Consciousness as Self-Modeling Dynamics: A Two-Layer Hypothesis of Integration, Self-Appropriation, and the Affective Synthesis (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21767269), hereafter the parent paper. That paper proposed a substrate-independent hypothesis in which five properties are derived from a single primitive (self-modeling closure), and it attached to several of them operational criteria: a split Lyapunov spectrum distinguishing a living core from a dead or disintegrated one; an operational distinction between valence that modulates a self-model’s dynamics and valence that merely shifts an output; an encoding-invariant closure threshold defined through mutual information at a fixed physical scale; and the claim that self-modeling closure can emerge under task pressure rather than being built in. Those criteria were asserted to be definable, non-empty, discriminating, and falsifiable; one of them (the closure threshold) drew a specific reviewer objection about encoding artifacts. The purpose of this work is to turn each asserted criterion into a demonstrated one, in isolated minimal simulations with declared failure conditions, and to do so without touching phenomenality, which the parent paper places outside the scope of a physical theory by a declared deflationary stance. We report four results and one transparently diagnosed-and-repaired confound.
